prompt: The same woman from the reference image, in the same plain studio with the same clothes and lighting, demonstrates a Tai Chi movement for beginners aged 50+. Movement: Grasp the Bird's Tail (Lan Que Wei), simplified ward-off and press, performed slowly to the right side. She shifts her weight to the left leg, turns slightly right and steps the right foot a small step forward into a shallow bow stance with the right knee only slightly bent above the right foot. The right forearm rises rounded in front of the chest, palm inward (ward off), while the left palm follows behind it; then both hands press gently forward at chest height, and she sits back onto the left leg while the hands draw back toward the chest. She then returns the right foot beside the left and lowers the arms to the sides. High stance only: knees bent only slightly (no more than about 30 degrees), each knee stays above its own foot and never collapses inward, back upright and tall, shoulders relaxed and down, chin level, calm gentle face, natural breathing. Very slow, smooth, continuous motion at a relaxed teaching pace with no pauses and no sudden changes. She begins and ends in exactly the neutral standing posture of the reference image (feet shoulder-width apart, arms relaxed at the sides) so the clip loops seamlessly. Static locked camera, no camera movement, no zoom, no cuts, full body always in frame from head to feet, feet visible on the floor, background unchanged.
